mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase does not correlate with subsequent economic weakness indicators.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent economic indicators of contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or INDPRO drop does not correlate with subsequent supply chain issues.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7%, the combination signals an accommodative monetary policy in a weak labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative policy in weak labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent consumer demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with subsequent market performance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 3% signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if the real GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is below 2%.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with slow GDP growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of high FEDFUNDS and low GDPC1 growth does not correlate with subsequent market performance.
